sources.note: Only two datapoints (9A velar nasal, 46A indefinite pronouns); none of the stress chapters 14A-17A code Ksingmul.

sources.citation: Cheeseman, Nathaniel, Paul Sidwell & Elizabeth Osborne. 2017. Khmuic linguistic bibliography with selected annotations. JSEALS 10(1).
sources.note: Bibliography only. Ksingmul-specific entries: Pram [Pogibenko] et al. 1990; Edmondson 2010; Ngô Đức Thịnh & Trương Văn Sinh 1973 (wordlists); Proschan 1996b (48-word comparison); Schliesinger profiles; Bradley 2010 p. 377. No Ksingmul phonology paper listed.

sources.citation: Edmondson, Jerold A. 2010. The Kháng language of Vietnam in comparison to Ksingmul (Xinh-mun). In K. A. McElhanon & G. Reesink (eds), A Mosaic of languages and cultures: studies celebrating the career of Karl J. Franklin, 138-154. SIL e-Books 19. Dallas: SIL International.
sources.note: Nothing on Ksingmul stress (the word 'stress' does not occur). p. 139 gives the general Mon-Khmer template 'weak-syllable (with reduction of vocalic and prosodic features) + strong-syllable (with maximum vowel and prosody differences)' (sesquisyllabic); p. 144 says Ksingmul is 'more preservative' and Ksingmul Nghệt 'retains the most sesquisyllabic structures'; p. 146 clusters arise when 'the vowel of weak first syllable, usually [ə] is syncopied'; Ksingmul initials of the main syllable cited from Pram et al. 1990:17; Kháng has six tones (p. 150). fetched sources from Wayback snapshot 20240731…

sources.citation: PHOIBLE 2.0, inventory Ksingmul (EA 2386), Dmitry Nikolaev, source 'Солнцев and Hoàng 1990'.
sources.note: 38 segments, no tones listed; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Pangloss Collection (CNRS-LACITO), 'Ksing Mun corpus': Michel Ferlus's 1983 vocabulary-elicitation recordings (Sơn La), with notes by Alexis Michaud.
sources.note: 'Ksing Mul is a non-tonal language'; 'The language does not have contrastive voiced stops.' Nothing on stress.

sources.note: Comparative lexicon; Ksinmul forms carry numeric marks (e.g. 'Kxinmul bɨ:ŋ.31'), which is what Edmondson 2010:144 calls 'Ksingmul forms with tone marking'; no stress statement.
